shortName: University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry
additionalCoursework: We require 12 credit hours in the humanities and/or the social or behavioral sciences and one year of expository writing. This may be met with English or non-science courses that involve expository writing. AP credit will not satisfy non-science requirements. We require that all science coursework be completed in-person for both the course and the lab (if applicable). An undergraduate degree is required from an accredited college or university. We prefer that science coursework be completed at a U.S. or Canadian college.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: URochester's Office of University Engagement and Enrichment seeks to create educational and programmatic opportunities through strategic collaborations for the University community to engage openly, learn continuously, and contribute meaningfully, while prioritizing respect, curiosity, well-being, and care. They focus on creating an environment that embraces a wide range of perspectives and ideas, that enhance learning, encourage critical thinking, and invite and deepen civil discourse to drive innovation, curiosity, and excellence.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Rochester has a Leave of Absence policy that covers a number of contingencies related to academic progress, health problems, or personal issues. Further information may be found in the Student Handbook at: http://www.urmc.rochester.edu/education/md/incoming-students/ under "Policies".
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: A wide variety of student enrichment programs in community engagement, outreach, global health, medical education and research complement our formal curriculum. Medical specialty interest groups, intramural athletics, artistic enrichment, and national societies provide additional opportunities for students. Multiple student initiated and organized community outreach programs exist to support the medical needs of our local communities. The Office of Medical Student Enrichment Programs incorporates oversight and funding opportunities for student initiated outreach, interest and affinity groups. The office also coordinates numerous academic events for the education of all students, assists with obtaining funding for summer and year-out research projects, and funding for international medicine summer, elective, or year-out experiences.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of Rochester is located in the City of Rochester, a diverse area of about 750,000 residents located in the scenic Finger Lakes region of New York. The medical school is part of the larger University of Rochester Medical Center and is located adjacent to the River Campus of the University of Rochester offering easy access to its cultural offerings and athletic facilities.  As one of the largest cities in New York, Rochester is big enough to offer an array of cultural, recreational and leisure activities, and small enough to live affordably and navigate easily.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The cost of living is significantly below the national average. Campus housing is available and assigned by lottery. High quality, affordable housing is located near campus and throughout the city. Housing is readily available and easy to find. Employment opportunities for spouses and partners abound and include engineering, education, health care and the arts.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
URSMD has a number of student enrichment groups where funding and faculty mentorship are available. 

The Paul J. Burgett Intercultural Center (BIC) is also a resource and aims to promote cultural understanding, build a community where everyone feels included, and provide avenues for promoting a culture of respect and opportunities for collaboration.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Disability Resources offers a variety of services for University of Rochester students, faculty, and staff. These services aim to provide an inclusive experience and equal access for students to academic content and program requirements. Our approach relies on collaboration among students, staff, and instructors.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry prioritizes student wellness and resilience through physical, emotional and mental, spiritual, intellectual, social, and financial wellness. There is a dedicated support team comprised of faculty and staff members, as well as the URSMD Wellness and Resilience Committee comprised of current medical school students from each class. Resources are shared on the Wellness and Resilience website, and in the Wellness Newsletter aimed to target the wellness needs of the student population at that time. 

Additional resources are available through the University Counseling Center.  The University Counseling Center provides an array of mental health services to students in a safe, caring, confidential, and culturally aware environment.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry, you benefit from a tight-knit, collaborative, humanities-focused educational environment, housed in a world-class research institution. Interprofessional teamwork is a hallmark of our culture.

The physicians at our medical center take an interdisciplinary approach to problem-solving—working closely with other experts on challenging cases and projects. We foster this same type of approach in our medical school.

Our students describe URochester as a place of unrivaled camaraderie, where professors are eager to collaborate with students. Our students learn that we not only prepare you for the science of your life's work, but the ART of your life's work.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Our medical school students can have a placement up to 45 minutes away from the medical school and must attest that they have a license and car prior to matriculation. Medical school students can't rely on the City of Rochester's public transit or ride share services.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students should dress in attire that is accepted as professional by the environment and patient population served. White coats required for patient encounters.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: A formal tutoring and learning assistance program is available and each student is assigned one of four Advisory Deans, who serve as mentors during the four-year medical school experience.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction the first day of class in their Introduction to Clinical Medicine course.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Hybrid including lectures, patient centered problem-based learning, team-based learning, flipped classrooms, hands on experiences, labs, and simulation.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Introduction to Clinical Medicine starts at the beginning of Phase 1.  Direct patient care begins the second semester of Phase 1.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: This 2-week course is designed to give selective students a brief, intense introduction to medical school.  Multiple factors are considered for selection.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: The following descriptors and approximate percentages will be used for Dean's Letter groupings: Outstanding (20%), Excellent (20%), Very Good (55%) and Good (5%).
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at whole class lectures is strongly encouraged, but not mandatory with exception of any exercise involving patients.  Recordings of lectures are available to students.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry's unique Double Helix: Translations and Transitions curriculum, is based on the concept that basic and clinical sciences should continuously inform each other. Courses are interdisciplinary and clinical exposure begins during the first week of school. Our curriculum emphasizes active student-centered learning in a curriculum based on competencies and outcomes to foster life-long learning. Clinical work is incorporated throughout the first two years and basic sciences are updated in the third and fourth years. A course unique to Rochester, Meliora in Medicine, exposes students to Collaborative Practice, Technology in Medicine, and Professional Identity Formation. Health humanities and bioethics are interwoven throughout this thread to continue our commitment to understanding medicine through the lens of human experience. We provide a supportive, challenging environment designed to foster collaboration, collegiality, and open communication rather than competition.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Students start Introduction to Clinical Medicine and Foundations of Biopsychosocial Practice in Year 1 incorporating full patient evaluations, screening and preventive care with physician preceptors. Second-year students participate in a Primary Care Clerkship. This is a core, longitudinal, continuity clerkship where working with physicians in adult and pediatric ambulatory practices is supplemented with core didactics and skills sessions. Ample electives in the last two years allow students to develop an individualized learning plan if they are interested in primary care. URochester does not track its students into primary care or specialty areas but allows and guides each student in deciding their own pathway toward excellence.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: URochester offers multiple, diverse opportunities to conduct research at our internationally recognized institution. Research opportunities are available starting during the first year.  Students can take advantage of multiple funding opportunities for summer research between Phase 1 and Phase 2. Funding is available for a research year-out through our Academic Research track.  In addition to allowing students to perform longitudinal meaningful research, this enrichment program provides opportunities for students to engage in elective learning and discussion sessions that prepare our graduates for future training in an academic career. A research master's degree is available in some departments under this program.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Final grades are by course years 1 and 2 which are graded pass/fail; and by clerkship/elective courses years 2, 3 and 4.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: The Distinction in Community Health is an option for students who make significant longitudinal contributions to community service and engage in learning about current issues in community health.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research is not a requirement, but nearly all of our students will participate in research while in medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Students rotate through diverse practice environments in the City of Rochester and at affiliated practices and hospitals in Upstate New York.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass/Fail non-clerkship courses; 
Honors/High Pass/Pass for clerkship courses

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: URSMD opened in 1925 on the campus of the University of Rochester Medical Center. Multiple diverse practice settings exist to help students explore different clinical environments and students have clinical experiences starting in the first year. Our mentorship programs are dedicated to helping students undergo the professional transformation required of future physicians and are spearheaded by our unique Advisory Dean system.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
At the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry (URSMD) we improve the health of individuals and populations through an innovative medical education program that emphasizes humility and growth. We inspire learners to become compassionate leaders in medicine and science by emphasizing collaboration, discovery and excellence.

We are guided by the core principle of Meliora, meaning “Ever Better.” We are a medical school where individuals achieve their highest objectives, unhindered by constraints on access, creativity, or participation. Our students are exposed to new opportunities and perspectives. Through the Double Helix Curriculum, early clinical experiences and our revolutionary biopsychosocial model, developing doctors who see not only disease, but the entire person. Mentored research, international experiences, pathways and community outreach opportunities complement our curriculum. We foster the knowledge, skills, and behaviors of the physician/scientist/humanist and combine evidence-based medical science with the relationship-centered art that is URochester medicine's distinctive trademark.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: REMS is an eight-year BA/BS + MD program for outstanding undergraduates who are committed to pursuing a medical career. As a REMS student, you’re admitted to the University’s School of Medicine and Dentistry once you successfully complete your bachelor’s degree and pre-med core courses. REMS students work closely with highly respected faculty members, attend special events, and gain hands-on experience in clinics and labs. High school applicants apply to this program through the undergraduate college at URochester.
medSchoolInformation.videoTitle: Welcome to the University of Rochester - School of Medicine & Dentistry

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: We require a criminal background check contracted through Certiphi, Inc.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: October 15-April 30: Two weeks.  May 1 - June 30: 5 days.  July 1 - 31: 2 days.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: A college's pre-health advisor letter or committee letter may substitute for individual letters.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A pre-health advisor or committee letter is preferred. If your school does not offer this, a minimum of 3 letters are required. We recommend 2 of the letters come from professors who have taught you.  This should include at least one letter from a professor in a science course.  A letter from a research setting or community outreach experience is recommended. If you have worked in a significant capacity to support yourself, a letter from your direct supervisor will augment your application.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interviews for the 2026-2027 admissions cycle will be virtual. Your interview day will consist of two individual interviews, and two group sessions. The group sessions include a live orientation with Dr. Christine Hay, Associate Dean for Admissions, and a group activity with a moderator.  Regular student panels and virtual tours led by our medical students will be offered, but are not required. Invited applicants will receive an email with further interview day details.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: August of the year prior to matriculation.  Interview invitations are sent via email.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two individual, conversational interviews and one 30 minute small group session.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be via Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All applicants when the verified AMCAS application is received.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: International students are only eligible to apply to our Levitan Endowed Family Scholarship (1 student annually).
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: We are a private medical school.  There is no state requirement.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: We are a private medical school.  There is no state requirement.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Canadian students are only eligible to our Levitan Endowed Family Scholarship (1 student annually).
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: International students are only eligible to our Levitan Endowed Family Scholarship (1 student annually).
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
URSMD medical students will have a strong foundation in science, evidence of curiosity through research/innovation, and demonstration of human connection through clinical experiences, community engagement, or the pursuit of the study of humanities.

Applications are reviewed from July through January. Interviews run from late August to mid-February.

Rochester has rolling admissions and offers begin mid-October. 

Waitlist activity typically begins at the end of April and as openings in the class occur, offers of admissions are extended (which traditionally can occur into July).
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We view MCAT scores holistically in context with other application materials.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: We view undergraduate, postbacc, and graduate GPAs holistically.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We have no minimum undergraduate GPA. We consider all GPAs holistically. We prefer graduate coursework in the hard sciences if an applicant has a softer undergraduate GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We have no minimum number of credit hours for postbacc or graduate work, but prefer when an applicant demonstrates they can do well with a full-time, rigorous course load.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept all community college coursework for applicants who start their education at a junior college and then transfer to a four-year institution and for applicants who take supplemental coursework at a community college. For applicants who have earned community college course credit as a high school student through an accelerated program, we require the coursework be re-taken at your undergraduate institution or used to advanced into upper-level courses.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of intent, letters of interest, and notices of significant updates may be sent via the applicant portal through the "additional documents" upload feature. We do not accept these letters and notifications via email.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: All applicants accepted to the University of Rochester School of Medicine & Dentistry must be able to meet the School’s technical standards. Students are required to review the standards and to sign a form certifying they have read, understand, and are able to meet the standards with or without reasonable accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Financial Aid office is committed to providing quality services to meet the needs of a diverse student population by offering financial resources and services to promote access to education and enhance student success by helping you to fund your education at the University of Rochester School of Medicine & Dentistry. We offer scholarships and long-term loans to students who demonstrate financial need. Entering students applying for institutional financial aid are required to provide a FAFSA, CSS profile, the School of Medicine's financial aid application, and various other verification and documentation forms.

The amount of assistance received is based upon analysis of family financial strength—the resources of student, spouse if married, and regardless of student age, marital, or IRS dependency status, parents. Parents are not required to provide financial support. While this information is used in determining scholarship eligibility, many students borrow additional resources in lieu of parental support. Applicants intending to seek scholarship assistance are urged to involve their parents early in the financial aid application process. Many families mistakenly assume that students at the graduate level will be aided without regard to parent circumstances and, while this may be typical for many graduate programs, it is not traditionally the case for professional programs.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Further information can be found in the Student Handbook at the following link: http://www.urmc.rochester.edu/education/md/incoming-students/ under "Policies"

medSchoolPrograms.info: Our Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) Program is a transformative ten-week experience designed to empower college students for careers in medicine and biomedical sciences. Selected from a national pool, participants engage in focused research, clinical rotations, problem-based learning sessions, and more under the guidance of faculty mentors.

Our combined MD/MBA degree program is a 5-year program.  Matriculants in this program complete their first year of study at the Simon School of Business, then spend 4 years in the School of Medicine and Dentistry and take additional electives for credit in both schools.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Commit to Enroll action becomes available.  If Rochester is your first choice and you have decided to attend medical school with us, we encourage you to select "Commit to Enroll" through AMCAS.  By selecting Commit to Enroll, you have withdrawn your application from all other medical schools.
Narrow acceptances to 1.  You are required to select "Plan to Enroll" if you are still holding your acceptance at Rochester.

Required to select 'Commit to Enroll' and withdraw applications from all other medical schools.  If an accepted applicant does not "Commit to Enroll" by the deadline, Rochester will rescind their acceptance.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Initial offers to waitlisted applicants begin the end of April.  As openings in the class occur, additional admission offers are made. Waitlist activity varies from year-to-year.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: URochester requires that students complete coursework in biology, chemistry, biochemistry, physics and mathematics to prepare them for the study of medicine. Because of our biopsychosocial emphasis, we expect that applicants will have a solid foundation in the social sciences and humanities, and demonstrate excellent communication skills. Physiology and anatomy, genetics, molecular biology, statistics and epidemiology all provide additional excellent grounding for medical school but are not required.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No limit, but we prefer to see some recent coursework if you have been out of undergrad for some time.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: URochester School of Medicine and Dentistry seeks students who exhibit a love of learning, have an appreciation of the science and art of medicine, empathize with the suffering of our communities, venture outside their comfort zone, and value a collaborative approach to problem solving.  URSMD is keenly aware of “distance traveled" by many of our applicants to reach this point of achievement in their academic career. Our holistic evaluation includes a careful examination of the academic record, letters of recommendation, the candidate's activities, and their personal statement within the backdrop of the resources and environment unique to each applicant. A strong academic record and good scores on the MCAT are necessary but not sufficient criteria for admission. Demonstrated excellence in a demanding academic program is expected and evidence of intrinsic intellectual drive, resilience, compassion and curiosity is highly valued.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We expect applicants to have familiarized themselves with the practice of medicine prior to applying.  Shadowing physicians in a variety of settings, scribing and medical assistantships where students work directly with physicians are excellent ways to observe medical practice. Sustained in-person experiences are particularly valued.  Applicants having only virtual shadowing experiences should seek out additional in-person opportunities if possible.
